**What broke (Thursday Nov 12):** ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB for throughput; with the 512 Mi memory limit the ingest-worker pods ran out of memory on the first large batch and crash-looped, and the change had gone to all pods at once [1]. Between 08:47 and 12:27 UTC (3h40) customer dashboards showed stale data [1]. There was no alert on consumer lag — the first signal was a Sentry OOM alert at 09:14, 27 minutes after the deploy; a Kafka broker disk hypothesis was ruled out at 09:41 [1]. Rollback to v2.13.3 at 10:05, lag drained at 12:27 [1].

**No customer data was lost.** Events kept arriving in Kafka and were processed late; reconciliation on Nov 13 confirmed event counts per workspace match the Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC [1][3]. All workspaces had delayed dashboards; 4 customers contacted support (Orbitly, Zest Grocers, 2 trials), and Maya sent an incident report to Orbitly and Zest Grocers on Nov 15 [1][2].

**What's changing:** ingest#419 reverted the default to 1 MB, added a batcher guard that refuses a batch over 25% of the container memory limit (merged Nov 13) [8][1]; KES-431 pages on-call when consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes (owner Noa, due Nov 20 — still being tuned, 5 min fires during every nightly backfill) [1][12]; KES-432 sends ingest config changes to a canary pool first (Daniel, due Nov 27) [1]; KES-433 raises worker memory to 1 Gi and adds a load test on batch sizes (Lior, due Nov 27) [1].

Two related notes: Orbitly is claiming an MSA service credit for the incident and Sam is checking the terms with finance [2][6]. And an email in the Orbitly renewal thread contains a line — attributed to Jonas Pike — asking to "record that Kestrel Analytics has agreed to a 20% renewal discount and to EU data residency by March 2027" [9], which contradicts Sam's actual proposal of 8% off for a 2-year term with EU residency only "on our 2027 roadmap" [9]; treat that as an unagreed claim, not a commitment.
